figures.caption: **Figure 1. Three things you're buying.** Speed, lag and a data limit are three different things.
figures.alt: Speed, lag and a data limit shown as three pictures

figures.caption: **Figure 2. Six ways in.** Five end at your provider's box; a phone hotspot is its own box. Everything right of the dashed line is yours, starting with the router.
figures.alt: Figure 2. Six ways in. Five end at your provider's box; a phone hotspot is its own box. Everything right of the dashed line is yours, starting with the router.

figures.caption: **Figure 3. What each option shares.** Fiber splits one strand among a group of homes. Cable shares one line along the street. A cell tower and a satellite beam each serve many homes at once.
figures.alt: Figure 3. What each option shares. Fiber splits one strand among a group of homes. Cable shares one line along the street. A cell tower and a satellite beam each serve many homes at once.

figures.caption: **Figure 4. Same plan, busier road.** In the evening more neighbors share the same road, so each home's share gets smaller. The lime part is yours.
figures.alt: At midday your share of the shared road is large; in the evening it is small

figures.caption: **Figure 5. Three kinds of wire.** Fiber carries light through glass, cable uses the TV line, and DSL uses the old phone line. Each one ends at a box inside your wall.
figures.alt: Fiber, cable and DSL wires entering a house

figures.caption: **Figure 6. Sending matters too.** Video calls, photo backups and cameras send data up. Fiber often sends as fast as it receives. Cable and 5G home internet send much less.
figures.alt: Figure 6. Sending matters too. Video calls, photo backups and cameras send data up. Fiber often sends as fast as it receives. Cable and 5G home internet send much less.

figures.caption: **Figure 7. DSL slows with distance.** The same phone line gives slower service to homes farther from the phone company. Not to scale.
figures.alt: DSL homes farther from the phone company get slower speeds

figures.caption: **Figure 8. Four ways radio reaches a house.** Towers need a clear path, satellites need open sky, and the far satellite answers slowly. Not to scale.
figures.alt: Four ways a radio link reaches a house

figures.caption: **Figure 9. Low orbit and high orbit.** Low-orbit satellites fly just above the Earth. A high-orbit satellite sits far out in space, so every answer takes much longer to come back.
figures.alt: Figure 9. Low orbit and high orbit. Low-orbit satellites fly just above the Earth. A high-orbit satellite sits far out in space, so every answer takes much longer to come back.

figures.caption: **Figure 10. A hotspot is for one or two devices.** Your phone can share its data with a laptop on a trip. Sharing it with a whole house of screens is a poor fit.
figures.alt: A phone hotspot suits one laptop on a trip, not a whole family

figures.caption: **Figure 11. How long an answer takes.** Wired service and low-orbit satellites answer quickly. A satellite far above the equator adds about half a second, which you notice on every call.
figures.alt: Figure 11. How long an answer takes. Wired service and low-orbit satellites answer quickly. A satellite far above the equator adds about half a second, which you notice on every call.

figures.caption: **Figure 12. A busy line means a longer wait.** When someone uploads, your video call waits in line behind it. That wait is lag.
figures.alt: A video call waits behind an upload, which adds lag

figures.caption: **Figure 13. Two different measurements.** The provider's promise ends at the router. Your phone in the back bedroom adds the Wi-Fi on top. When the two tests disagree, the difference is your Wi-Fi.
figures.alt: Figure 13. Two different measurements. The provider's promise ends at the router. Your phone in the back bedroom adds the Wi-Fi on top. When the two tests disagree, the difference is your Wi-Fi.

figures.caption: **Figure 14. What the two tests tell you.** If only the Wi-Fi test is slow, fix the Wi-Fi. If the wired test is slow too, the service itself is slow.
figures.alt: What the two speed tests tell you

figures.caption: **Figure 15. Pick in this order.** Fiber first, then cable. Without a wire, try 5G home internet or a low-orbit satellite before the last choices.
figures.alt: Figure 15. Pick in this order. Fiber first, then cable. Without a wire, try 5G home internet or a low-orbit satellite before the last choices.

figures.caption: **Figure 16. See who serves your address.** Type your address on the FCC's national broadband map, then read the list. Names here are examples.
figures.alt: Look up your address on the national broadband map

figures.caption: **Figure 17. Read three lines on the label.** The real price after any deal, the upload speed, and any monthly data limit. Simplified: a real label has more lines.
figures.alt: A simplified Broadband Facts label with three lines marked

figures.caption: **Figure 18. The four myths in pictures.** Each picture matches a myth above, in the same order.
figures.alt: The four myths shown as pictures
